title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

story.what: TypeCollector now sends every analyzer diagnostic through a filter that reports it only when its location is in source and in a syntax tree of the compilation being analyzed. Two places that used to index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly now use safe lookups: the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull property diagnostic and the field MemberNeedsKey diagnostic. Properties and fields that come from metadata therefore no longer throw. New generator tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image, reference it from a [MessagePackObject] consumer, run the analyzers and the generator, and check that the resolver source is produced. The change also adds README and MsgPack004 docs, plus an unrelated edit to MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer for string keys.
story.why: When a member type was a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly, the collector walked that type's members. Those members have no syntax references, so indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] threw IndexOutOfRangeException. The build showed this only as AD0001 and CS8785 warnings, and the assembly got no generated resolver (MP-2283).

findings.title: String keys lose collision-resistant comparer under UntrustedData
findings.detail: GetEqualityComparer<T> in the runtime library now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default for T == string even when HashCollisionResistant is true. Before, it returned the SipHash-based StringEqualityComparer. MP-2283 is about the generator and analyzer and does not ask for this change. Its effect: with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, a dictionary or hash set built from string keys taken from the payload uses the default string hash again. Crafted keys could then slow those collections down (hash-flooding DoS), which is exactly what this setting exists to prevent. The doc remarks at lines 128-130 still say a collision-resistant comparer is returned, and HashResistantCache still maps string to StringEqualityComparer, so the code and the docs now disagree. No test covers this change.

findings.title: Analyzer filter silently drops every diagnostic without a source location
findings.detail: The fix only needs to skip diagnostics about members defined in metadata. Instead, ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wraps every report and drops any diagnostic whose location is not in source in the current compilation. That includes diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None), for example PartialTypeRequired with a null primaryLocation, or MessageFormatterMustBeMessagePackFormatter when the argument syntax cannot be found. Before, these were still reported without a location; now they vanish with no trace. For a closed generic type from metadata, the consuming project now generates the formatter itself (CollectGeneric collects OriginalDefinition), yet all diagnostics about that type's members are hidden. A public unkeyed member is therefore silently left out of the formatter in the consuming assembly. ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember locks this in by expecting no diagnostics. This conflicts with N1, which says failures must not pass silently. Limit the filter to diagnostics that do have a location outside the compilation, or report something to the consumer.

findings.title: No check that the formatter for the closed generic struct is generated
findings.detail: F3 requires the consuming assembly to get its resolver and a formatter for the member type, as it would for a same-project generic. The new tests skip the generated-sources check and only assert that the resolver file's hint name exists. A resolver file would probably be emitted even if no formatter for MyGenericStruct<T> or Item<T> were collected, so the tests do not show that the cross-assembly generic type is actually registered and formatted. No snapshot under Resources records the expected output.

findings.title: No runtime round-trip test for a cross-assembly closed generic struct
findings.detail: The expectation for F3 includes serializing and deserializing an instance whose member is a closed generic struct from another assembly, using the generated resolver. No runtime or integration test does this, so it is unverified that the consumer-generated formatter for a metadata struct works at runtime. That formatter now skips the struct's private backing fields, which metadata exposes.
